I have an interview in a few hours. I'm practicing some answers to interview questions and trying not to get nervous.
What interview tips do you have?
Be sure to ask about what benefits they offer. Who their medical insurance is with. Do they offer any matching with 401k if they offer it.

Ask questions about the company and position. You are interviewing them as much as they are you. Ask why the position is open. If the person left, ask why. If the person was promoted ask how long they had their previous position before being promoted. Inquire about employee turnover and longevity. Ask what the overall goals of the company are. Mainly, let the interviewer/s know that you are looking for a good fit for you as much as they are for them.
ask that fucker who interviews you what they like about (working for) dis company and if they say something like diversity, then run away.
Don't drink a 40 of Olde English, smoke a blunt and then get all sweaty skateboarding in the parking lot for 30 minutes before you go in for the interview.

Do the interview like you don't even need the job. Don't be a jerk, or act disinterested. Be cordial, and ask questions, but act like you're not relying on them giving you an offer.

Even when i'm employed, I continue to apply and interview for other positions.

I've noticed that when interviewing for jobs, while I already have a job i'm happy with I tend to get a lot more offers. Its probably because the lack of needing that job makes me more relaxed, and confident throughout the interview.

So if you can convince yourself that you don't need the job you're interviewing for, you'll be more relaxed and confident in the interview.

Make sure you look at their website if they have one, and mention something about it. Like I noticed you have x amount of employees, or x amount of offices after looking at your website. Appears as if you have interest in the company and that you can research independently.
If you don't have any face or neck tattoos, draw some on with a Sharpie. That's the kind of street cred that reputable employers look for!
When the interview is over ask the interviewer if there is any reason why they wouldn't hire you. Then follow up with "it helps me better myself". It's not much but it's something

Get ready to answer "trick questions"

"What would be your biggest downfall/hindrance?"

... I pay a little too much attention to detail, and sometimes people think I am working slower because of that. I love being thorough!
Know the details and history of the company, make yourself prepared, be confident at yourself, and smile.
